text: I learned tracking skills from Kamala.
She is the best hunter in the district.
She doesn't approve of me going too far alone.
I go anyway, sometimes.
Satyapala says I'll get myself killed if I ignore the boundaries.
I think he's too cautious.
Tarala and I sometimes follow animal trails together.
We have found paths that are not on any known routes.
I do not always report them.
Some discoveries feel like they need more time before being shared.
Certain forest zones feel quieter than others.
Not empty — quiet.
Animals behave differently in those zones.
I once followed a herd into a high path leading toward the upper terraces.
That path was partially collapsed but still passable.
I didn't tell Satyapala.
My father's brother died in a felling accident years ago, when a sal tree came down wrong in the monsoon.
Satyapala never talks about it directly.
I think that shaped his wariness of the forest.
Kamala records animal movement patterns.
I sometimes look at her notes without permission.
Patterns sometimes repeat in ways that feel intentional.
I have not told her this.
Chapala once said the platform has routes that aren't roads.
I think I understand what he meant.
The forest edge shifts slightly over time.
I am not sure anyone else notices.
I sometimes feel like I am being led somewhere when I track alone.
I cannot explain this.
But I follow it anyway.
